input.quote: All other liability is expressly waived and released as a condition of, and consideration for, the execution of this Agreement by the Servicer or the Marketing Agent, as applicable. Each of the Servicer and the Marketing Agent, severally and not jointly, will be liable only for its own willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in performing its obligations under this Agreement.
input.rationale: This securitization TSA contains no monetary limitation of liability at all, and that absence works in our favour. Cellco's exposure as Servicer/Marketing Agent (§ 6.2(a), p0283) and its indemnities to the Issuer, Owner Trustee and Indenture Trustee (§ 6.3(a), p0291-p0292) are unlimited in amount, so the indemnification, wilful misconduct, bad faith and gross negligence heads the playbook wants carved out of any cap in fact sit outside any cap. Our side is limited rather than exposed: the Depositor's liability is subject to the mirror-image standard in § 5.2(a) (p0243) and § 9.6 Limited Recourse (p0378) confines claims against the Depositor and the Issuer to the Depositor Transferred Property. The culpability standard is mutual as between the transaction parties, and p0469 bars punitive and consequential damages in arbitration for both sides, matching the mutual consequential-damages exclusion in the preferred position. None of the walk-away triggers is present — there is no Vendor-only cap, no sub-6-month cap, and no indemnities inside a cap. Noted but not flagged: there are no express confidentiality, data-protection or third-party IP carve-outs and no USD floor (the framework is uncapped, so a floor is unnecessary), and Cellco is answerable only for wilful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence rather than ordinary negligence — a market-standard servicer standard in ABS transactions and a sub-element short of preferred wording rather than a material failure. Proposing a monetary cap here would introduce a ceiling on our recovery against Cellco where none exists, so no redline.
